title: A Journey from Lahore
description: A family's journey from pre-Partition Lahore to present-day Delhi, remembered across three generations.

journey.description: Asha Devi grows up in Lahore, in a home near the old city where her father ran a small cloth shop.
The family crosses the newly drawn border on foot during Partition, arriving in Amritsar with only what they could carry.
The family resettles in Ludhiana, rebuilding their livelihood in the growing textile trade.
The next generation now lives in Delhi, and shares Asha Devi's story so it is not forgotten.

title: Phulkari — Mere Nani Ki Ungliyon Ki Kala
description: A granddaughter documents the vanishing hand-embroidery technique of Phulkari, passed down through three generations of women in her family.

title: Jalandhar Ke Boliyaan
description: Traditional Punjabi boliyaan (folk verses) sung during harvest season, recorded live at a village gathering near Jalandhar.

title: Kashi Ka Kaam — Hoshiarpur Wood Inlay
description: A third-generation artisan demonstrates Hoshiarpur's centuries-old wood inlay (kashi) craft, now practised by fewer than a dozen families.

title: Vaisakhi Mele Ki Paramparaa
description: Residents describe how the Vaisakhi fair at Anandpur Sahib has evolved over decades while keeping its core rituals and community spirit alive.

title: From Sialkot to Chandigarh
description: A demo migration story tracing one family's path from Sialkot through Jammu to the newly built city of Chandigarh.

journey.description: Karam Singh's family runs a small sports-goods workshop in Sialkot, a craft the city was already known for.
The family flees to Jammu during Partition, joining a refugee camp before deciding where to settle permanently.
The family moves to the newly planned city of Chandigarh, finding work as the city expands.
Three generations later, the family still lives in Chandigarh and keeps the memory of Sialkot alive through old photographs and recipes.

title: From Rawalpindi to Delhi
description: A demo migration story following a family's crossing from Rawalpindi through Attari and Jalandhar to Delhi.

journey.description: Rukhsana Bibi's family lives near Rawalpindi's old bazaar, where her father worked as a schoolteacher.
The family joins a refugee convoy crossing at Attari during the Partition migrations of 1947.
The family spends nearly a decade in Jalandhar, where Rukhsana Bibi's father resumes teaching at a local school.
Her grandchildren now live in Delhi and are recording her story as part of a family history project.
